item.description:
PressTalk 0.1.28
Personal Vocabulary now shows the complete collection of saved corrections in a two-column list: recognized phrase and preferred spelling. Every saved rule is applied. Selecting a row chooses which entry to edit or remove.
Add spelling appends another entry; one spelling can have several recognized phrases, entered on separate lines. The editor retains its selection and makes newly added entries visible. Existing vocabulary data is preserved without migration. The previous dropdown also applied all saved rules, but its single visible selection made that behavior unclear.
The optional Write numbers as digits setting from 0.1.27 remains disabled by default. No recognition model, dependency, licence or permission reset. Existing settings and local speech models are retained.
Signed automatic updates are available from 0.1.26 onward. Users of 0.1.25 and earlier need one manual installation. The known first-recording AirPods retry issue remains under investigation. Explicit main-language locking and a Parakeet Ultra comparison remain separate planned work.
Apple Silicon · macOS 14 or later. Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple.

PressTalk 0.1.27
New Settings option: Write numbers as digits. It is disabled by default. Enable it to format clear English and German number phrases locally: “ninety nine problems” becomes “99 problems”, “zweiundzwanzig” becomes “22”. Clear decimal phrases are supported too.
Turning it off keeps the recognizer's original number formatting. Quotes, code, addresses, existing digits and saved Personal Vocabulary stay literal. Ambiguous digit sequences and unsupported forms can stay words. This does not infer phone numbers, rewrite units or format dates.
No speech-model or dependency update. Dictation still uses local Parakeet v3 with the processor choice in Settings. No audio or transcripts are uploaded for number formatting. Explicit main-language locking is still planned separately.
Existing licences, settings and models are retained. Signed automatic updates are available from 0.1.26 onward; users on 0.1.25 and earlier need one manual installation. Automatic checks/downloads can be disabled in Settings. The existing first-recording AirPods retry issue remains under investigation.
Apple Silicon · macOS 14 or later. Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple.

PressTalk 0.1.26
Clear English/German email addresses and websites are formatted automatically: “hello at example dot com” becomes hello@example.com. Ordinary uses of “at” are protected.
Clear vocal hesitations such as “uh” and “ähm” are removed in ordinary dictation. English “um” is removed when the rest of its sentence is confidently English; ambiguous short phrases retain the word. Meaningful words, quoted text, addresses and matching saved vocabulary phrases stay intact. Hesitation-only recordings finish quietly.
Fn + Space starts hands-free dictation; press it again to finish. Quick accidental key taps no longer speak a recognizer rejection as a backend error.
Settings offers Neural Engine/CPU or GPU/CPU processing, local Personal Vocabulary corrections, optional spoken formatting commands, and signed automatic app updates. Updates wait for dictation and clipboard restoration to finish.
Your existing licence and settings are retained. Users of 0.1.25 and earlier need one manual installation of this release to receive the updater. Automatic checks and downloads can be disabled in Settings. No account is required for dictation, and no audio or transcripts are sent by the updater.
Speech models are unchanged. General conversion of spoken German numbers into digits is not included. The existing first-recording AirPods retry issue remains under investigation.
Apple Silicon · macOS 14 or later. Signed with Developer ID, notarized by Apple.
